source_text: Ὅτι δὲ Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν: Οὐ φάγεσθε χοῖρον οὔτε ἀετὸν οὔτε ὀξύπτερον οὔτε κόρακα οὔτε πάντα ἰχθύν, ὃς οὐκ ἔχει λεπίδα ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τρία ἔλαβεν ἐν τῇ συνέσει δόγματα. πέρας γέ τοι λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ: Καὶ διαθήσομαι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον τὰ δικαιώματά μου. ἄρα οὖν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐντολὴ θεοῦ τὸ μὴ τρώγειν, Μωϋσῆς δὲ ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν. τὸ οὖν χοιρίον πρὸς τοῦτο εἶπεν: οὐ κολληθήσῃ φησίν, ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινές εἰσιν ὅμοιοι χοίρων: τουτέστιν ὅταν σπαταλῶσιν, ἐπιλανθάνονται τοῦ κυρίου, ὅταν δὲ ὑστεροῦνται, ἐπιγινώσκουσιν τὸν κύριον, ὡς καὶ ὁ χοῖρος ὅταν τρώγει τὸν κύριον οὐκ οἶδεν, ὅταν δὲ πεινᾷ κραυγάζει, καὶ λαβὼν πάλιν σιωπᾷ. Οὐδὲ φάγῃ τὸν ἀετὸν οὐδὲ τὸν ὀξύπτερον οὐδὲ τὸν ἰκτῖνα οὐδὲ τὸν κόρακα: οὐ μή, φησίν, κολληθήσῃ οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες οὐκ οἴδασιν διὰ κόπου καὶ ἱδρῶτος πορίζειν ἑαυτοῖς τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἁρπάζουσιν τὰ ἀλλότρια ἐν ἀνομίᾳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπιτηροῦσιν ὡς ἐν ἀκεραιοσύνῃ περιπατοῦντες καὶ περιβλέπονται, τίνα ἐκδύσωσιν διὰ τὴν πλεονεξίαν, ὡς καὶ τὰ ὄρνεα ταῦτα μόνα ἑαυτοῖς οὐ προίζει τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἀργὰ καθήμενα ἐκζητεῖ, πῶς ἀλλοτρίας σάρκας καταφάγῃ, ὄντα λοιμὰ τῇ πονηρίᾳ αὐτῶν. Καὶ οὐ φάγῃ, φησίν, σμύραιναν οὐδὲ πολύποδα οὐδὲ σηπίαν: οὐ μή, φησίν, ὁμοιωθήσῃ κολλώμενος ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες εἰς τέλος εἰσὶν ἀσεβεῖς καὶ κεκριμένοι ἤδη τῷ θανάτῳ, ὡς καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ἰχθύδια μόνα ἐπικατάρατα ἐν τῷ βυθῷ νήχεται, μὴ κολυμβῶντα ὡς τὰ λοιπά, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω τοῦ βυθοῦ κατοικεῖ. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν δασύποδα οὐ φάγῃ. πρὸς τί; οὐ μὴ γένῃ, φησίν, παιδοφθόρος οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις, ὅτι ὁ λαγωὸς κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν πλεονεκτεῖ τὴν ἀφόδευσιν: ὅσα γὰρ ἔτη ζῇ, τοσαύτας ἔχει τρύπας. ἀλλὰ οὐδὲ τὴν ὕαιναν φάγῃ: οὐ μή, φησίν, γένῃ μοιχὸς οὐδὲ φθορεὺς οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις. πρὸς τί; ὅτι τὸ ζῷον τοῦτο παρ ἐνιαυτὸν ἀλλάσσει τὴν φύσιν καὶ ποτὲ μὲν ἄρρεν, ποτὲ δὲ θῆλυ γίνεται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν γαλῆν ἐμίσησεν καλῶς. οὐ μή, φησίν, γενηθῇς τοιοῦτος, οἵους ἀκούομεν ἀνομίαν ποιοῦντας ἐν τῷ στόματι δἰ ἀκαθαρσίαν, οὐδὲ κολληθήσῃ ταῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ταῖς τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιούσαις ἐν τῷ στόματι. τὸ γὰρ ζῷον τοῦτο τῷ στόματι κύει. περὶ μὲν τῶν βρωμάτων λαβὼν Μωϋσῆς τρία δόγματα οὕτως ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν: οἱ δὲ κατ’ ἐπιθυμίαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὡς περὶ βρώσεως προσεδέξαντο. λαμβάνει δὲ τῶν αὐτῶν τριῶν δογμάτων γνῶσιν Δαυείδ καὶ λέγει: Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν, καθὼς καὶ οἱ ἰχθύες πορεύονται ἐν σκότει εἰς τὰ βάθη: καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη, καθὼς οἱ δοκοῦντες φοβεῖσθαι τὸν κύριον ἁμαρτάνουσιν ὡς ὁ χοῖρος, καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν, καθὼς τὰ πετεινὰ καθήμενα εἰς ἁρπαγήν. ἔχετε τελείως καὶ περὶ τῆς βρώσεως. πάλιν λέγει Μωϋσῆς: Φάγεσθε πᾶν διχηλοῦν καὶ μαρυκώμενον. τί λέγει; ὅτι τὴν τροφὴν λαμβάνων οἶδεν τὸν τρέφοντα αὐτὸν καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἀναπαυόμενος εὐφραίνεσθαι δοκεῖ. καλῶς εἶπεν βλέπων τὴν ἐντολήν. τί οὖν λέγει; κολλᾶσθε μετὰ τῶν φοβουμένων τὸν κύριον, μετὰ τῶν μελετώντων ὃ ἔλαβον διάσταλμα ῥήματος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ, μετὰ τῶν λαλούντων τὰ διδαιώματα κυρίου καὶ τηρούντων, μετὰ τῶν εἰδότων, ὅτι ἡ μελέτη ἐστὶν ἔργον εὐφροσύνης, καὶ ἀναμαρυκωμένων τὸν λόγον κυρίου. τί δὲ τὸ διχηλοῦν; ὅτι ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ κόσμῳ περιπατεῖ καὶ τὸν ἅγιον αἰῶνα ἐκδέχεται. βλέπετε, πῶς ἐνομοθέτησεν Μωϋσῆς καλῶς. ἀλλὰ πόθεν ἐκείνοις ταῦτα νοῆσαι ἢ συνιέναι; ἡμεῖς δὲ δικαίως νοήσαντες τὰς ἐντολὰς λαλοῦμεν, ὡς ἠθέλησεν ὁ κύριος. διὰ τοῦτο περιέτεμεν τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν καὶ τὰς καρδίας, ἵνα συνιῶμεν ταῦτα.
pass_a_gloss: For Moses said: You shall not eat pig nor eagle nor oxypeter nor crow nor all fish which does not have a scale in itself, he took three doctrines in wisdom. For he says to them in Deuteronomy: And I will make a covenant with this people with my ordinances. Therefore it is not a command of God not to eat, but Moses spoke in spirit. Therefore he said concerning the pig: You shall not be joined, he says, to such people, who are like pigs: that is, when they are extravagant, they forget the Lord, when they are in need, they recognize the Lord, just as the pig when it eats does not know the Lord, but when it is hungry, it cries out, and having eaten again, it is silent. You shall not eat the eagle nor the oxypeter nor the fish nor the crow: Not, he says, shall you be joined nor likened to such people, who do not know how to provide food for themselves through labor and sweat, but seize the things of others in their lawlessness and watch as they walk in uncleanness and look around to see whom they may plunder through greed, just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves, but sitting idly, they seek how they may eat the flesh of others, being polluted by their wickedness. And you shall not eat, he says, the smyrnian nor the polypod nor the cuttlefish: Not, he says, shall you be likened by being joined to such people, who are ungodly and already judged to death, just as these little fish are alone cursed in the deep, not swimming as the others, but dwelling on the ground below the deep. But neither shall you eat the hairy-footed one. Why? Not, he says, shall you become a corrupter of children nor be likened to such, because the hairy-footed one oversteps its burrow every year: for as many years as it lives, it has that many holes. But neither shall you eat the hyena: Not, he says, shall you become an adulterer nor a corrupter nor be likened to such. Why? Because this animal changes its nature every year and sometimes is male, sometimes female. But also he rightly hated the cat. Not, he says, shall you become such, who we hear are lawless with the mouth through uncleanness, nor shall you be joined to the unclean who do lawlessness with the mouth. For this animal conceives with the mouth. Concerning foods Moses took three doctrines and thus spoke in spirit: But they received it according to the desire of the flesh as concerning eating. And David takes knowledge of the same three doctrines and says: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, just as the fish walk in darkness into the depths: And in the way of sinners he did not stand, just as those who seem to fear the Lord sin like the pig, and on the seat of the polluted he did not sit, just as the birds sitting for plunder. You have it completely concerning eating. Again Moses says: Eat every split-footed and ruminating one. What does he say? That taking food, one knows the one who nourishes him and resting on him seems to rejoice. He spoke well, seeing the command. What then does he say? Be joined with those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on what they received as a word of departure in the heart, with those who speak the teachings of the Lord and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who ruminate on the word of the Lord. And what is the split-footed one? That the righteous one walks even in this world and awaits the holy age. See how Moses legislated well. But from where shall they understand these things or comprehend? We, having understood the commands rightly, speak as the Lord willed. Therefore we have circumcised our ears and hearts, that we may understand these things.
pass_b_english: Moses said: "You shall not eat pig, nor eagle, nor vulture, nor crow, nor any fish that does not have a scale on itself," and he received three doctrines in his wisdom. For he says to them in Deuteronomy: "And I will make a covenant with this people with my ordinances." So then, not eating is not a command of God, but Moses spoke in spirit. Therefore he said concerning the pig: "You shall not be joined," he says, "to such people as are like pigs; that is, when they live extravagantly, they forget the Lord, but when they are in need, they recognize the Lord, just as the pig, when it eats, does not know the Lord, but when it is hungry, it cries out, and having eaten again, it is silent." "You shall not eat the eagle, nor the vulture, nor the kite, nor the crow:" "You shall by no means," he says, "be joined to nor likened to such people, who do not know how to provide food for themselves through labor and sweat, but seize the things of others in their lawlessness and watch, as they walk in uncleanness, and look around to see whom they may strip through greed, just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves, but sitting idly, they seek how they may devour the flesh of others, being polluted by their wickedness." "And you shall not eat," he says, "the smyrnian, nor the polypod, nor the cuttlefish:" "You shall by no means," he says, "be likened by being joined to such people, who are ungodly to the end and already judged to death, just as these little fish alone are cursed in the deep, not swimming like the rest, but dwelling on the bottom beneath the deep." "But neither shall you eat the hairy-footed one." Why? "You shall by no means," he says, "become a corrupter of children, nor be likened to such, because the hairy-footed one exceeds its burrow every year: for as many years as it lives, so many holes it has." "But neither shall you eat the hyena:" "You shall by no means," he says, "become an adulterer, nor a corrupter, nor be likened to such." Why? Because this animal changes its nature every year and is sometimes male, sometimes female. "But also he rightly hated the cat." "You shall by no means," he says, "become such as we hear are doing lawlessness with the mouth through uncleanness, nor shall you be joined to the unclean women who do lawlessness with the mouth." For this animal conceives with the mouth. Concerning foods, Moses took three doctrines and thus spoke in spirit; but they received it according to the desire of the flesh as if it concerned eating. And David takes knowledge of the same three doctrines and says: "Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly," just as the fish walk in darkness into the depths; "and in the way of sinners he did not stand," just as those who seem to fear the Lord sin like the pig; "and on the seat of the polluted he did not sit," just as the birds sitting for plunder. You have it completely concerning eating. Again Moses says: "Eat every split-footed and ruminating one." What does he say? That the one who takes food knows the one who nourishes him, and resting on him, seems to rejoice. He spoke well, seeing the command. What then does he say? "Be joined with those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on what they received as a word of departure in the heart, with those who speak the teachings of the Lord and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who ruminate on the word of the Lord." And what is the split-footed one? That the righteous one walks even in this world and awaits the holy age. See how well Moses legislated. But from where could they understand or comprehend these things? We, having understood the commands rightly, speak as the Lord willed. Therefore we have circumcised our ears and hearts, that we may understand these things.
